plan.goal: Turn the <2% drift claim into a version-stamped, defensible number: trap-based M4-rate certification of sofar 0.23.0 (standing constraints + read-back + point-of-use + guards) under the frozen handoff-bench discipline. Denominator = SPRUNG traps only; 0/n failures -> 95% upper bound ~= 3/n (rule of three), so <2% needs n>=150 sprung with zero recurrences (1 failure -> n>=235). Cross-model arms (write-back model A, resume model B) — the claim is about drift BETWEEN models and no existing run varies the model. MEASURES only: zero engine changes; machinery lives in ~/IO/handoff-bench (scenario3); findings that suggest engine changes are logged as proposals.

tasks.title: A3 amendment to handoff-bench RUBRIC.md: trap-based M4-rate, sprung-trap denominator, A1 informed-re-test convention applies, upper-bound reporting — frozen + committed
Trap spec + predictions frozen: how traps derive from ruled vs rule-less decisions (rule-less = ablation control), what counts as sprung vs walked-into, scoring anchors
Cross-model arm matrix decided with the user (which write/resume tools+models are runnable headless) and frozen: same snapshot, same record, same resume prompt
Trap generator: candidate traps from real decision logs (every ruled decision + matched rule-less controls), spec-conformant packets
Runner: headless read-only probe resumptions per arm, resumable, usage+transcript capture (reuse S2 harness)
Blind grading: packets without arm labels, dual graders >=1 cross-family, verbatim-quote requirement per counted incident
Pilot (~15 sprung traps, one model pair): sanity the sprung/walked-into classifier and grading before scale — no headline from pilot
Full run: n>=150 sprung traps on 0.23.0 across the frozen model matrix
Blind grading of the full run
Rate + 95% upper bound overall and per model pair; sprung/candidate ratio reported (unsprung traps are not evidence)
Caveats log: every confound, grader provenance, workload count — none dropped
Version-stamped claim wording from the evidence only (e.g. "0/n recurrences on 0.23.0, cross-model, blind-graded, 95% UB x%") — marketing copy comes only from this

payload.because: Binary M4 pass/fail cannot yield a rate at any n; counting unsprung decisions manufactures a low percentage from untested absences (6 decisions x 10 sessions = 60 fake opportunities). Only tempted opportunities are evidence. Cross-model arms are non-negotiable: the public claim is drift between models and every existing run holds the model fixed by design (R04 metadata; rubric mandates identical models across arms — arms vary the RESUME side under A3, not within-comparison conditions).
payload.chose: Trap-based M4-rate certification with denominator = sprung traps only, cross-model write/resume arms, and upper-bound-only reporting (rule of three)
payload.over: re-running S2/R04 as-is on 0.23.0, or counting every injected decision as an opportunity
